strings.meta.title: Open BitLocker and Linux Drives on macOS — Lukotta
strings.meta.description: Open BitLocker, NTFS, LUKS and Linux drives on your Mac. Type the password and the drive appears in Finder, readable and writable. Free and open source.
strings.meta.ogTitle: Lukotta — BitLocker, Linux and VM disks on macOS
strings.meta.ogDescription: Plug in a drive or open a disk image, type the password, and it appears in Finder, readable and writable, like any other disk.

strings.hero.title: Open BitLocker, Linux and virtual machine disks on macOS.
strings.hero.subtitle: Plug in a drive or open a disk image and type the password, and it appears in Finder. Readable and writable, like any other disk.
strings.hero.meta: Version {version} · Apple Silicon · macOS 15 Sequoia or later
strings.hero.screenshotAlt: The Lukotta window on macOS, listing the drives connected to the Mac and what each one holds.
strings.how.title: How It Works
strings.how.lead: macOS cannot read BitLocker or Linux filesystems. Linux can. Lukotta starts a small Linux virtual machine, unlocks the drive inside it, and hands the drive back to Finder.
strings.how.1.title: Plug in the drive
strings.how.2.title: Type the password
strings.how.2.body: A volume password, a LUKS passphrase, or a 48-digit BitLocker recovery key.
strings.how.3.title: Open it in Finder
strings.how.3.body: The volume appears under Locations, and reads, writes and ejects like any other drive.
strings.features.title: Features
strings.features.lead: Lukotta opens drives and disk images that macOS refuses to read, and gives them to Finder as ordinary volumes.
strings.features.body: It takes physical drives and image files alike. A BitLocker volume opens with its password or with a 48-digit recovery key, and BitLocker and NTFS volumes are both read and written, so files can be copied onto a drive as well as off it.
strings.features.body2: Any drive or image can be opened read-only instead, and Lukotta can reopen whatever was open the last time you were logged in.
strings.formats.title: Supported formats
strings.formats.bitlocker.note: Unlocked with the volume password or a 48-digit recovery key
strings.formats.lvm.note: Several volumes on one drive unlock together
strings.formats.ntfs.note: Including a volume Windows left dirty or hibernated
strings.formats.vmdkStream.note: What an OVA carries. Written in one pass, so it cannot be changed in place
strings.formats.specs: Every format in full detail, including how each one is read and written
strings.formats.experimental: Support for these formats is experimental. Writing to them has not been extensively tested.
strings.formats.not.title: Not supported
strings.formats.not.1: FileVault and encrypted disk images, which macOS opens itself
strings.formats.not.2: Drives sealed to a TPM rather than a password, including Ubuntu's newer hardware-backed encryption
strings.formats.not.3: LUKS volumes whose header is stored away from the drive
strings.formats.not.5: An image that names another file: a VMware snapshot chain, a differencing VHD, or a qcow2 with a backing file
strings.name.title: The Name
strings.name.body: Lúkotta is Finnish for “without a lock”, from {lukko}, a lock, with the ending {tta} marking the absence of something. The stress falls on the first syllable, as it always does in Finnish.
strings.faq.title: FAQ
strings.faq.1.a: Nothing. It is free to download and free to use. There is no paid version, no subscription, no trial that runs out and no account to make.
strings.faq.1.a2: It is also free software, under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. The source is public: you can read it, build it yourself, change it, and pass on what you change.
strings.faq.2.a: Yes, and write to them. Type the volume password or paste a 48-digit recovery key, and the drive opens in Finder.
strings.faq.3.q: Can Lukotta write to NTFS drives?
strings.faq.3.a: Yes. Files copy onto an NTFS drive as well as off it.
strings.faq.4.a: Yes. ext2, ext3, ext4, btrfs and XFS open, plain or inside LUKS encryption. A drive laid out with LVM opens all its volumes together.
strings.faq.5.q: Can Lukotta open a virtual machine's disk?
strings.faq.5.a: Yes, without starting the machine. Open a qcow2, VMDK, VDI, VHD or VHDX image and copy files out of it, or into it.
strings.faq.6.q: Does Lukotta run on an Intel Mac?
strings.faq.6.a: No. It needs the virtualisation Apple Silicon provides.
